searchText: Any new thoughts on address size increase or statelessness or state expiry from anyone here? I have a question. Can we recover most `LONG` (untruncated 32 byte) addresses by doing a full sync? I know that we only have `SHORT` addresses for externally-owned accounts with zero nonce. Are there any other cases? I think the problem is that contracts contain 20 byte addresses in a lot of contexts (eg. your ERC20 balance) So we can't do some kind of in-place swap easily I agree, it is a complicated problem. I am just trying to determine which long addresses we have and don't have. In your magician's post, you mention a translation table. Maybe we can prefill it. hmm, that would require a sudden mass storage change, which we don't have the tools to do I don't think it's worth the effort Or, hold on, is the plan that even existing 20 byte addresses get converted to new-style, together with the translation table approach for existing contracts? Yes, the system would store 32 byte addresses, and truncate them for legacy opcodes. hmm I would like to decide which addresses we don't have 32 bytes for. We only have 20 byte addresses for EOAs with zero nonce. Any others? not-yet-created counterfactual contracts eg. Argent is switching to that for their wallets Aha, yes.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Any new thoughts on address size increase or statelessness or state expiry from anyone here?

excerpts.author: pauld.9606
excerpts.content:
I have a question.

Can we recover most `LONG` (untruncated 32 byte) addresses by doing a full sync?

I know that we only have `SHORT` addresses for externally-owned accounts with zero nonce. Are there any other cases?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: I think the problem is that contracts contain 20 byte addresses in a lot of contexts (eg. your ERC20 balance)

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: So we can't do some kind of in-place swap easily

excerpts.author: pauld.9606
excerpts.content: I agree, it is a complicated problem. I am just trying to determine which long addresses we have and don't have.

excerpts.author: pauld.9606
excerpts.content: In your magician's post, you mention a translation table. Maybe we can prefill it.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: hmm, that would require a sudden mass storage change, which we don't have the tools to do

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: I don't think it's worth the effort

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Or, hold on, is the plan that even existing 20 byte addresses get converted to new-style, together with the translation table approach for existing contracts?

excerpts.author: pauld.9606
excerpts.content: Yes, the system would store 32 byte addresses, and truncate them for legacy opcodes.

excerpts.author: pauld.9606
excerpts.content: I would like to decide which addresses we don't have 32 bytes for. We only have 20 byte addresses for EOAs with zero nonce. Any others?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: eg. Argent is switching to that for their wallets
